dossier.orientation: Papier's academic-year diary (Aug–Jul) is a paper diary with weekly overviews, term timetables and deadline/grade trackers that the buyer personalises with their own name and, optionally, a custom title, choosing a week-to-view or day-to-view layout and a hardback or spiral binding.

setup_conditions: Name and optional custom diary-title personalisation is selected and applied during the purchase flow (E3).
decision_gaps: Does the calendar-year diary format carry the same deadline/grade trackers, term timetables and diary-title personalisation documented for the academic-year diary?
What is the price of the academic-year diary itself (no price evidence was captured for this specific product line)?
What is the recommended order-by date to receive a personalised academic-year diary before the August start of the academic year?
defining_need_fit.supported_core_workflow: A single paper diary that shows weekly/term structure at a glance, tracks deadlines and grades, and feels personally theirs rather than generic.
defining_need_fit.caveat: This fit is established for the documented academic-year (Aug–Jul) diary; the calendar-year alternative mentioned in the workflow is not covered by the selected evidence and is not required for the academic-year branch to be addressed.
defining_need_fit.why: E1 defines the academic-year structure, E2 supplies the weekly/term overview plus deadline and grade trackers, E3 supplies name/title personalisation, and E5/E4 document the layout and binding choices the workflow requires — together these cover every required capability listed for this audience.

ranked_relevance.why: Directly matches the stated need: weekly overviews, term timetables and deadline/grade trackers give the at-a-glance weekly/term structure and tracking the audience wants in one diary.
Name and diary-title personalisation is the documented mechanism that makes the diary feel 'personally theirs rather than generic', the core differentiator this audience is weighing.
Establishes the academic-year (Aug–Jul) format that anchors the diary's term structure, the format half of the audience's stated academic-vs-calendar comparison.
Documents the week-to-view vs day-to-view layout choice the workflow explicitly requires the buyer to make.
Documents the hardback-vs-spiral binding/size choice that is part of the same purchase decision alongside layout.
Because personalised diaries aren't normally returnable, this 30-day satisfaction remedy is the licensed mechanism that offsets the purchase risk of personalising ahead of the year.
An unattributed, weakly-sourced handwriting-memory claim; true and licensed but too thin to present to this solution-aware, comparison-shopping audience as a reason to choose paper.
FSC-certified, sustainably sourced paper is a real but background trust fact, not central to the weekly-structure/personalisation decision this audience is making.

problem_fits.caveat: E3 confirms name (and title) personalisation generally but does not state how non-standard spellings, special characters or culturally diverse names are handled, so accurate rendering for this specific sub-group is not established by the selected evidence.
problem_fits.why: Name/title personalisation is a documented, licensed capability relevant to this problem, but the ledger only proves the feature exists, not that it resolves the specific accuracy concern raised.

segment_objections.objection: Personalising the cover with a name/title is usually irreversible if there's a mistake or a change of mind, which is a real risk when buying months ahead of the academic year.
segment_objections.answer: Returns on personalised products aren't typically accepted, but customers can get in touch within 30 days of the order date and it will be sorted out.

segment_objections.objection: Buyers with non-standard or culturally diverse name spellings may doubt the personalisation will render their name accurately, a friction point this specific group has raised about personalised goods generally.
